nodes.label: Patient has had headache, dizziness, and imbalance for 2 years
Patient is a 44-year-old man with a history of hypertension and cervical disc herniation; one year ago he underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
Patient's father had progressive cognitive decline and imbalance since age 50 and died of cerebral hemorrhage at age 65
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes and bilateral Babinski sign
MRI shows lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities
Patient may have cerebral amyloid angiopathy contributing to chronic cerebrovascular disease
MRA and carotid ultrasound were not retrieved, leaving vascular stenosis unassessed
Patient may have intracranial or carotid artery stenosis contributing to chronic cerebrovascular disease
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy as the predominant subtype of chronic cerebrovascular disease
Hypertensive arteriolosclerosis/small vessel disease as a contributor to chronic cerebrovascular disease
Intracranial or carotid artery stenosis as a contributing subtype of chronic cerebrovascular disease
Cortical superficial siderosis and anticoagulant history could not be evaluated on available imaging and records
Radiologist analysis prioritizes cerebral amyloid angiopathy as the predominant subtype based on lobar-dominant microbleeds and familial hemorrhage history
Patient may have hereditary/familial cerebral amyloid angiopathy
